lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 4 you met helping verbs. In "She is running", which word is the helping verb? Is: it helps the main verb, running.
Perfect tenses use a form of have with a past participle, like walked, eaten or gone.
Present perfect: I have walked (it happened, and it matters now). Past perfect: I had walked (before another past event). Future perfect: I will have walked (done before a time in the future).
Examples: By the time the bus came, we had walked home. By Friday, I will have finished my book. I have seen that film twice.
Keep tenses consistent: don't switch from past to present in the middle of a story. Not: She opened the door and sees a fox. But: She opened the door and saw a fox.
Try it in the world: before you stop playing, tell a friend what you have built today, and what you will have finished by next time. Next: conjunctions, prepositions and interjections.

exercises.prompt: Which is the present perfect?
exercises.hint: The present perfect uses have or has, not had or will.
exercises.explain: "I have walked" is the present perfect.

exercises.prompt: Which is the past perfect?
exercises.explain: "She had eaten" is the past perfect.

exercises.prompt: Which helper verb do the perfect tenses use?
exercises.hint: Look at the lesson's three perfect tenses. Which small verb is in all of them?
exercises.explain: The perfect tenses all use a form of have: have, has, had or will have.

exercises.prompt: "I will have finished" is the future perfect.
exercises.explain: Yes: that is the future perfect.

exercises.prompt: Choose: "I ___ already seen that film."
exercises.hint: Which word goes with "seen" to say it happened before now?
exercises.explain: "I have already seen" is the present perfect.

exercises.prompt: Choose: "By the time the bus came, we ___ home."
exercises.explain: The walking finished before the bus came: past perfect.

exercises.prompt: Choose: "By Friday, I ___ my book."
exercises.explain: Done before a future time: future perfect.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence keeps its tenses the same?
choices: She opened the door and saw a fox.
She opened the door and sees a fox.
She opens the door and saw a fox.
exercises.explain: Opened and saw are both past.

exercises.prompt: "He jumped and runs away" keeps its tenses consistent.
exercises.explain: No: it should be "He jumped and ran away".

exercises.prompt: Which is correct?
exercises.hint: Say each one aloud. Which uses the right form of have with gone?
choices: They have gone to the park.
They have went to the park.
They has gone to the park.
exercises.explain: "They have gone" is correct.

exercises.prompt: Which tells about something finished before another past event?
choices: The film had started when we arrived.
exercises.explain: The film started before we arrived: past perfect.

exercises.prompt: Fix the tenses: "Yesterday we build a den and eat in it."
choices: Yesterday we built a den and ate in it.
Yesterday we build a den and ate in it.
Yesterday we built a den and eat in it.
exercises.explain: Built and ate are both past, to match yesterday.

exercises.prompt: Choose: "By next summer, Ava ___ to swim."
exercises.explain: Done before a future time: will have learnt.

exercises.prompt: "I have eaten" means the eating is finished.
exercises.explain: Yes: the perfect tenses show finished actions.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order.
exercises.explain: By noon we had climbed the hill: past perfect.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence to its tense.
exercises.hint: Look at the helper: have, had, will have, or none.
exercises.explain: Have walked: present perfect. Had walked: past perfect. Will have walked: future perfect. Walked: simple past.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences: are the tenses consistent?
items: She opened the door and saw a fox.
We ate and then we slept.
They build a den and played in it.
exercises.hint: Find both verbs. Are they both in the past?
exercises.explain: Opened and saw, ate and slept match. Jumped and runs, build and played switch tense.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences by their perfect tense.
exercises.hint: Look at the helper: have or has, had, or will have?
exercises.explain: Have or has: the present perfect (have seen, have eaten). Had: the past perfect (had left, had finished). Will have: the future perfect (will have gone, will have won).

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence to what it means.
items: By noon, I will have finished.
matches: done before a noon now past
done before a noon to come
exercises.hint: Look at the helper: will have looks ahead, had looks back, and have means now.
exercises.explain: Will have finished: it will be done before a noon still to come. Had finished: it was done before a noon in the past. Have finished: it is done, and that matters now.

exercises.prompt: How many verbs must change to keep the tenses the same? "Yesterday I wake up, eat my breakfast and ran to school."
exercises.hint: Yesterday tells you every verb should be in the past. Check each one.
exercises.explain: Yesterday needs the past: wake becomes woke and eat becomes ate; ran is already past. So 2 verbs change: Yesterday I woke up, ate my breakfast and ran to school.
